subject: Re: BrightAnalytics - SLO & monitoring clarifications
messages:
From: Sara Choi <sara.choi@brightanalytics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Jones <tim.jones@brightanalytics.com>
Date: 2025-11-09 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: BrightAnalytics - SLO & monitoring questionnaire

Hi Connor,

Thanks for taking our onboarding call earlier. Procurement asked us to send the attached questionnaire to capture how you measure availability and latency for hosted inference endpoints. A few points we need clarified before legal can sign:

- How is "availability" measured (per-region, per-model, per-route)? What window and aggregation method is used for the % uptime number?
- Do you sample traffic for high-volume routes? If so, what's the sampling strategy and how long do you retain raw samples?
- What alerting thresholds do you expose to customers (both SRE-facing and customer-facing)? Are there configurable hooks/contacts?
- For customers requesting dashboard access, what's the entitlement model and what data is redacted in read-only views?
- If Redwood requests a temporary SLA exception (e.g., during a migration or scheduled capacity maintenance), what is the formal exception request path and who signs off?

Attached: BrightAnalytics_SLO_Questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx)

We'd appreciate draft answers and any sample dashboards or screenshots you can share. Legal is aiming to wrap this week.

Thanks,
Sara

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sara Choi <sara.choi@brightanalytics.com>
Cc: Tim Jones <tim.jones@brightanalytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-09 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: BrightAnalytics - SLO & monitoring questionnaire

Sara — thanks for the questionnaire and the clear list. Attaching a first-pass answers PDF and a short notes file with links to the dashboard we typically grant read-only access to. High level answers below; see attached for the table-by-table responses.

- Availability measurement: we measure per-region and per-route. The primary uptime SLO is computed from successful request rate (2xx/3xx) over rolling 30d windows and also reported as a 7d rolling window for near-term ops. We compute per-route error rate and combine by weight of traffic to produce account-level availability.
- Sampling: we do not sample the control path for SLO calculations; we compute based on full aggregated counters. For very high-volume customers (>1B tokens/month) we may use sampled detailed traces for investigatory tooling, but the SLO math uses aggregated counters to avoid sampling bias. Raw traces are retained for 30 days by default; metrics aggregates are retained 13 months.
- Alerting thresholds: we publish SRE-facing alerts (e.g., error-rate > 1% for 5m, latency p95 > X ms for 10m) and provide a customer-facing incident/state feed (status.redwood.ai) and webhook notifications. Customers can request additional webhook endpoints to receive alerts for their account.
- Dashboard access: we provide a read-only Grafana view scoped to the customer account/regions. The read-only view redacts user-identifying request payloads and any PII; request-level logs remain in our internal system (accessible via legal/approved audit).
- Exception path: we have a formal exception request process — customer rep opens a ticket with procurement@redwood.com, attaches the reason, duration, and rollback plan. Exceptions are reviewed by Product + SRE for technical risk and by Legal for contract impact. Temporary SLA exceptions are approved at director level or higher for customer-impacting changes.

Attached: Redwood_SLO_Responses_v1.pdf (pdf), Redwood_dashboard-readonly-invite.txt (txt)

I'll leave Karthik on the thread for any technical follow-ups about aggregation or sampling. If legal wants a short amendment template for the exception clause we can provide a redline.

Best,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-09 18:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: BrightAnalytics SLO detail + temporary-exception guidance

Connor / Priyom — quick internal note tied to the questionnaire Connor sent:

- On aggregation: confirm we include 5xx/4xx as failures. For multi-region customers we compute region-level SLOs and an account-level SLO that is a traffic-weighted average. Call this out explicitly in the response table; Sara's procurement team is asking for per-region guarantees.
- Sampling clar: we should emphasize that SLO math uses full counters not sampled traces; sampling only applies to deep traces for debugging.
- Exception path: procurement occasionally asks for 99.99% wording; our standard hosted SLA for the tier discussed is 99.95% monthly availability. We can offer a targeted short-term 99.99% behavioral commitment as an exception (e.g., for 60 days during cutover) but only if the customer agrees to an operational playbook and compensating capacity commit. That needs Product director sign-off (I can route).

Action items for Connor: 1) Update the PDF to call out the monthly and 7d windows explicitly and note failure classes. 2) Propose the exception text (60-day extra-commit + playbook) and include an amendment template link.

Link to draft amendment: https://redwood.app/docs/sla-amendment-template/BA-137-draft
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/BA-137

-Karthik

Connor — thanks for the quick turnaround and the detailed responses. We've reviewed the PDF and the notes Karthik added. A couple short items:

- The per-region measurement approach is acceptable; legal would like the definition of "downtime" spelled out in the amendment (we'll mark as contract language).
- BrightAnalytics is willing to accept a 60-day elevated-availability exception to reach an effective 99.99% if Redwood provides the operational playbook and the directed capacity commit. Can you confirm the playbook will be shared prior to amendment signing?
- Please send a read-only dashboard invite with the following access: east-us and west-us regions only; account-level SLO graphs and the 30d/7d windows. A short README on what is redacted would help our security reviewers.

If you can put the amendment and playbook links into DocuSign we can route internally this week.

Appreciate the coordination — file attached confirming questions list and acceptance.

Best,
